questions.q:
Four gas cylinders containing $\mathrm{He}, \mathrm{N}_2, \mathrm{CO}_2$ and $\mathrm{NH}_3$ gases separately are graudally cooled from a temperature of $500 \mathrm{~K}$. Which gas will liquify first ?
(Given $\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{C}}$ in $\mathrm{K}-\mathrm{He}: 5.3, \mathrm{~N}_2: 126, \mathrm{CO}_2: 304.1$ and $\left.\mathrm{NH}_3: 405.5\right)$
questions.solution:
Higher is the critical temperature, easier is the liquefaction of gas.
The order of liquefaction of gases will be:
$\mathrm{NH}_3\gt \mathrm{CO}_2\gt \mathrm{N}_2\gt \mathrm{He}$
Hence, among the given gases $\mathrm{NH}_3$ has the highest critical temperature. Therefore, it will be liquefied first.

T_B & =200 \mathrm{~s} \\

\frac{r_B}{r_A} & =\sqrt{\frac{M_A}{M_B}}=\frac{V_B T_A}{T_B \cdot V_A} \\

\end{aligned}$

questions.solution: The decrease in viscosity at high temperature is due to molecules having high kinetic energy, which allows them to overcome intermolecular forces and slip past one another.

questions.solution: On increasing the temperature, the most probable speed of gas molecules increases.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the cause of the net attractive force on a molecule at the surface of a liquid?
questions.solution: The net attractive force on a molecule at the surface of a liquid is caused by the molecules below it.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Why do liquids wet things and spread across their surfaces as a thin film?
questions.solution: Liquids wet things and spread as a thin film across their surfaces because of surface tension.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the significance of the slope of the lines obtained at different pressures in Charles' law?
options: The slope is not significant in Charles' law.
The slope indicates a direct relationship between volume and temperature.
The slope determines the molar mass of the gas.
The slope changes with each measurement, making it unreliable.
questions.solution: The slope of the lines obtained at different pressures indicates the direct relationship between volume and temperature as described by Charles' law.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When does the clear boundary between the liquid and vapor phases disappear?
options: When the liquid becomes more dense than the vapor
When the vapor becomes denser than the liquid
When the density of the liquid and vapors becomes the same
questions.solution: The clear boundary between the liquid and vapor phases disappears when the density of the liquid and vapors becomes the same.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: If the temperature, volume, and pressure of a fixed amount of gas change from T1, V1, and p1 to T2, V2, and p2, what can be written based on the ideal gas equation?
questions.solution: The ideal gas equation can be written as p1V1/T1 = p2V2/T2 when the temperature, volume, and pressure of a fixed amount of gas change.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the temperature in Kelvin (K) equivalent to 0°C on the Celsius scale?
questions.solution: 0°C on the Celsius scale is equal to 273.15 K on the Kelvin scale.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the consequence of having more energy in the molecules on the surface of a liquid?
questions.solution: Molecules on the surface have more energy, which leads to increased vapor pressure.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Is the value of 'a' in the van der Waals equation dependent on temperature and pressure?
options: It depends on the gas's color
It depends on the gas's atomic number
questions.solution: The value of 'a' is independent of temperature and pressure, indicating that it does not depend on these factors.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How does viscosity change as temperature increases in a liquid?
questions.solution: Viscosity decreases as the temperature of a liquid rises.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Why do liquids have a definite volume?
options: Because their molecules are separated from each other
Because their molecules have strong chemical bonds
Because their molecules do not separate from each other
questions.solution: Liquids have a definite volume because their molecules do not separate from each other.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the ideal gas constant, R, also called?
questions.solution: The ideal gas constant, R, is also called the Universal Gas Constant because it is the same for all gases.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is suggested about gases in relation to their critical temperature and liquifaction?
options: Gases liquify when heated above their critical temperature.
Gases need to be heated to liquify.
Gases should be cooled below their critical temperature for liquifaction.
Gases can liquify at any temperature.
questions.solution: Gases should be cooled below their critical temperature for liquifaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When do repulsive forces between gas molecules become significant?
questions.solution: Repulsive forces between gas molecules become significant at high pressures.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What occurs when an evacuated container is partially filled with a liquid?
options: The liquid evaporates to fill the remaining volume with vapor.
The liquid separates into its constituent elements.
questions.solution: When an evacuated container is partially filled with a liquid, a portion of the liquid evaporates to fill the remaining volume with vapor.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In what conditions are the partial pressures of gases calculated according to Dalton's law?
questions.solution: According to Dalton's law, the partial pressures of gases are calculated at constant temperature and volume.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the behavior of the pV vs. p plot for real gases at constant temperature?
options: It is always a straight line
It shows significant deviation from ideal behavior
It is not influenced by pressure changes
It behaves like an ideal gas
questions.solution: The pV vs. p plot for real gases at constant temperature exhibits a significant deviation from ideal behavior.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What determines the Boyle point of a gas?
questions.solution: The Boyle point of a gas depends on the nature of the gas.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which material is an "extremely viscous liquid" with properties resembling solids?
questions.solution: Glass is an extremely viscous liquid with properties that resemble solids.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: At what point do repulsive forces between gas molecules become significant?
options: When molecules are almost in contact
When the temperature is extremely high
When the gas is in a gaseous state
questions.solution: Repulsive forces between gas molecules become significant when molecules are almost in contact.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the expenditure of energy required to increase the surface area of a liquid by one unit defined as?
questions.solution: The energy required to increase the surface area of a liquid by one unit is defined as surface tension.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the mathematical representation of Avogadro's law, indicating the relationship between volume (V) and the number of moles (n) of gas?
questions.solution: Avogadro's law can be mathematically represented as V/n = constant, where "n" is the number of moles of the gas.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Who demonstrated that the actual distribution of molecular speeds depends on temperature and molecular mass?
questions.solution: Maxwell and Boltzmann showed that the distribution of molecular speeds depends on temperature and molecular mass.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What happens to Z values below Boyle temperature for real gases?
options: Z decreases as pressure increases, reaching a minimum value.
Z shows negative deviations from ideality.
questions.solution: Below Boyle temperature, real gases first show a decrease in Z value with increasing pressure, reaching a minimum value.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Why do different particles in a gas have different speeds and kinetic energies?
options: Due to a loss of kinetic energy
As a result of molecular collisions
questions.solution: Different particles in a gas have different speeds and kinetic energies because of the collisions they undergo.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Why do real gases deviate from the ideal gas law?
options: Real gases have a different molecular composition.
Real gases are not subject to high pressures.
Molecular interactions between gas molecules come into play at high pressures.
Real gases have a different temperature range.
questions.solution: Real gases deviate from the ideal gas law because at high pressures, molecules of gases are very close to each other, leading to molecular interactions that affect the pressure exerted by the gas.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: According to kinetic theory, what is assumed to be directly proportional to the absolute temperature?
questions.solution: Kinetic theory assumes that the average kinetic energy of gas molecules is directly proportional to the absolute temperature.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the Ideal gas equation often referred to as?
questions.solution: The Ideal gas equation is often called the "equation of state" because it describes the state of any gas.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How is a gas below its critical temperature that can be liquified by applying pressure referred to?
questions.solution: A gas below its critical temperature that can be liquified by applying pressure is called a vapor of the substance.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What conditions must be met for the equation V = nRT/p to be applicable to any gas?
questions.solution: The equation V = nRT/p is applicable to any gas when the behavior of the gas approaches ideal behavior.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What determines the vapor pressure of a liquid?
questions.solution: The process of vaporization is temperature-dependent, so the temperature must be mentioned when reporting the vapor pressure of a liquid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What causes the change in the speed and energy of gas molecules?
questions.solution: The change in the speed and energy of gas molecules is caused by their continuous motion and collisions with each other and with the walls of the container.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Who obtained the first complete data on pressure-volume-temperature relations of a substance in both gaseous and liquid states?
questions.solution: The first complete data on pressure-volume-temperature relations of a substance in both gaseous and liquid states was obtained by Thomas Andrews.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What happens to the initial uniformity of particle speeds in a gas?
options: It changes due to a loss of kinetic energy
It is disrupted by molecular collisions
It becomes constant at a particular temperature
questions.solution: The initial uniformity of particle speeds in a gas is disrupted by molecular collisions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Why is it possible for the distribution of speeds of gas particles to remain constant?
options: Because gas particles are uniform in size
Because gas particles collide in a predictable manner
Because molecular collisions do not affect particle speeds
Because even though individual speeds change, the distribution remains the same
questions.solution: The distribution of speeds of gas particles remains constant because, although individual speeds change, the overall distribution does not.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How do gas molecules with heavier mass compare to those with lighter mass at the same temperature?
options: They have the same most probable speed
questions.solution: At the same temperature, gas molecules with heavier mass move slower than those with lighter mass.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Under what conditions do real gases show ideal behavior in terms of pressure?
questions.solution: Real gases exhibit ideal behavior when pressure approaches zero.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the consequence of gas particles being in constant and random motion?
options: The gas has a fixed shape
The gas particles are at rest
The gas particles occupy fixed positions
The gas does not have a fixed shape
questions.solution: The constant and random motion of gas particles results in a gas that does not have a fixed shape.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What results from the random motion of gas particles?
options: A fixed shape for the gas
Collisions between particles and container walls
questions.solution: The random motion of gas particles results in collisions between the particles and the walls of the container.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the result of compression at constant temperature for all gases?
options: Gases show the same behavior as carbon dioxide.
questions.solution: All gases, upon compression at constant temperature, show the same behavior as shown by carbon dioxide.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of deviation follows the minimum value of pV in the pV vs. p plot for gases like carbon monoxide and methane?
questions.solution: After reaching a minimum value, the pV value in the pV vs. p plot for gases like carbon monoxide and methane starts increasing, showing a positive deviation from ideal behavior.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the interpretation of the volume of a gas being zero at -273.15°C according to Charles' law?
options: The gas is in its gaseous state.
questions.solution: According to Charles' law, when the volume of a gas is zero at -273.15°C, it means the gas no longer exists (disappears).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What mathematical relationship between pressure and temperature is described by Gay Lussac's law?
questions.solution: Gay Lussac's law states that at constant volume, the pressure of a fixed amount of gas varies directly with the temperature, indicating a direct relationship between pressure and temperature.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What happens to the vapor pressure as liquid evaporates into a partially filled container?
questions.solution: Initially, as the liquid evaporates, the pressure exerted by vapors on the container's walls (vapor pressure) increases.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What happens to the layer of molecules in immediate contact with a fixed surface when a liquid flows over it?
options: The layer retreats from the surface
questions.solution: When a liquid flows over a fixed surface, the layer of molecules in immediate contact with the surface remains stationary.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What does Avogadro's law state regarding the relationship between the volume of gases, the number of molecules, and the conditions of temperature and pressure?
options: Equal volumes of all gases contain an equal number of molecules.
Volume is inversely proportional to the number of molecules.
Gases with different volumes have the same number of molecules.
Volume depends on temperature, not the number of molecules.
questions.solution: Avogadro's law states that equal volumes of all gases under the same conditions of temperature and pressure contain an equal number of molecules.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the mathematical expression of Boyle's law?
questions.solution: The mathematical expression for Boyle's law is " p ∝ 1/V ( at constant T and n)."

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How does an increase in temperature affect the kinetic energy of molecules?
options: It has no effect on kinetic energy
It causes a slight increase in kinetic energy
questions.solution: An increase in temperature increases the kinetic energy of molecules.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What term is used to describe both a liquid and a gas, recognizing their continuity?
questions.solution: The term "fluid" is used to recognize the continuity between a liquid and a gas.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the behavior of the pV vs. p plot for carbon monoxide and methane initially?
questions.solution: The pV vs. p plot for carbon monoxide and methane initially shows a negative deviation from ideal behavior, where the pV value decreases with increasing pressure.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What property of liquids gives them a stretching property on their surface?
questions.solution: Surface tension is the property of liquids that gives them a stretching property on their surface.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How do real gases behave when their molecules are very close to each other?
options: They experience a decrease in temperature.
questions.solution: Real gases deviate from ideal behavior when their molecules are very close to each other due to the onset of molecular interactions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: At what temperatures do intermolecular forces become significant for real gases?
questions.solution: Interactions between gas molecules become significant at low temperatures.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What does the symbol "k<sub>1</sub>" represent in the Boyle’s law equation?
questions.solution: "k<sub>1</sub>" is the proportionality constant in the equation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How does the behavior of real gases change as the temperature is lowered?
options: They become more like ideal gases.
They remain in the gaseous state at all temperatures.
They show considerable deviation from ideal behavior.
questions.solution: As the temperature of real gases is lowered, their behavior changes, and they show considerable deviation from ideal behavior.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the mathematical expression for the compressibility factor Z?
questions.solution: The mathematical expression for the compressibility factor Z, which is Z = pV/nRT.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Why does a molecule on the surface of a liquid experience a net attractive force towards the interior of the liquid?
questions.solution: A molecule on the surface of a liquid experiences a net attractive force towards the interior of the liquid due to surface tension.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: At what temperature does the volume of a gas reach zero, according to Charles' law?
questions.solution: According to Charles' law, the volume of a gas reaches zero at -273.15°C.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What does the symbol "u" represent in the equation for average speed?
questions.solution: The symbol "u" represents the individual speeds of gas molecules in the equation for average speed.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is viscosity a measure of?
questions.solution: Viscosity is a measure of resistance to flow.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the behavior of gas particles at ordinary temperature and pressure?
options: There is no force of attraction between them
questions.solution: Gas particles at ordinary temperature and pressure are assumed to have no force of attraction between them.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What does Dalton's law of partial pressure state?
options: The total pressure is always greater than the sum of the partial pressures.
The total pressure is less than the sum of the partial pressures.
The total pressure is equal to the sum of the partial pressures.
The total pressure is unrelated to the partial pressures.
questions.solution: Dalton's law of partial pressure states that the total pressure exerted by a mixture of non-reactive gases is equal to the sum of the partial pressures of individual gases.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What are the constants 'a' and 'b' in the van der Waals equation called?
questions.solution: Constants 'a' and 'b' in the van der Waals equation are referred to as van der Waals constants.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What does the proportional constant (η) measure in terms of fluid properties?
questions.solution: The proportional constant (η) measures the viscosity of a fluid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What does the value of "k1" vary with according to Boyle’s law?
questions.solution: The value of "k1" varies only with temperature.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the Greek letter denoted for surface tension?
questions.solution: Surface tension is denoted by the Greek letter γ (Gamma).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What do the values of freezing temperature and atmospheric pressure represent in the context of STP?
options: The conditions for ideal gas behavior
questions.solution: Freezing temperature and atmospheric pressure represent the conditions for ideal gas behavior at STP.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When can liquid and gas be distinguished from each other?
options: When the fluid is below its critical temperature and pressure
When the fluid is above its critical temperature and pressure
When the fluid is in a vacuum
questions.solution: Liquid and gas can be distinguished from each other when the fluid is below its critical temperature, and its pressure and volume lie under the dome, where liquid and gas are in equilibrium.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the mathematical relationship described by Boyle's law?
questions.solution: Boyle's law is p1V1 = p2V2, which represents the relationship between initial and final pressures and volumes.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the boiling temperature called at 1 bar pressure?
questions.solution: If the pressure is 1 bar, the boiling point is called the standard boiling point of the liquid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the vapor pressure called when an equilibrium is established between the liquid and vapor phase?
questions.solution: The vapor pressure at the stage of equilibrium is known as saturated vapor pressure.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What does an increase in pressure do to liquid carbon dioxide?
options: It changes the color of the liquid.
questions.solution: An increase in pressure simply compresses the liquid carbon dioxide.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the behavior of gas molecules at close distances?
options: Gas molecules exhibit strong attractive forces.
questions.solution: Gas molecules must have forces of repulsion between them to prevent squashing in tiny volumes, implying that they repel each other.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What are gases considered to be in terms of mass?
questions.solution: Gases are considered as point masses, meaning their individual mass and volume are negligible.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How is Boyle's law graphically presented?
options: Pressure versus volume at different temperatures
Volume versus temperature at different pressures
Volume versus pressure at different temperatures
questions.solution: The graph of Boyle's law shows the relationship between pressure and volume at different temperatures.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Why doesn't boiling occur when a liquid is heated in a closed vessel?
options: Because the liquid becomes more dense
Because the temperature does not increase
Because the liquid and vapor densities become the same
questions.solution: Boiling does not occur when a liquid is heated in a closed vessel because the vapor pressure increases, indicating that the vapor pressure must increase for boiling to take place.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is obtained by taking the square root of the mean of the square of speeds?
questions.solution: Taking the square root of the mean of the square of speeds gives the root mean square speed.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What did Charles and Gay Lussac's experiments reveal about the volume of a gas at constant pressure?
options: The volume decreases with increasing temperature.
The volume increases with increasing temperature.
The volume decreases with decreasing temperature.
questions.solution: The experiments of Charles and Gay Lussac showed that for a fixed mass of gas at constant pressure, the volume of the gas increases with increasing temperature.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the relationship between kinetic energy and the striking of gas particles on the container walls?
options: Kinetic energy decreases with increased striking
Kinetic energy increases with increased striking
questions.solution: When a gas is heated, the kinetic energy of the particles increases, and as a result, they strike the walls of the container more frequently, thus exerting more pressure.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the term used to describe each line on the graph of pressure vs temperature (Kelvin) graph at constant molar volume?
questions.solution: Each line on the graph is referred to as an isochore.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the effect of variable speed on the kinetic energy of gas molecules?
options: It has no effect on kinetic energy
It results in variable kinetic energy
questions.solution: Variable speed of gas molecules leads to variable kinetic energy.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What happens to the layer of molecules above a chosen layer in a flowing liquid?
questions.solution: The layer of molecules above a chosen layer in a flowing liquid accelerates its flow.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is required for the liquifaction of so-called permanent gases?
questions.solution: Liquifaction of so-called permanent gases requires both compression and cooling.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the behavior of gases at high pressures with respect to Boyle's law?
options: Gases follow Boyle's law more closely at high pressures.
Gases deviate from Boyle's law at high pressures.
Gases become more compressible at high pressures.
Gases have lower volumes at high pressures.
questions.solution: At high pressures, gases deviate from Boyle's law, indicating that they do not follow it closely under such conditions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When do real gases exhibit ideal behavior?
questions.solution: Real gases exhibit ideal behavior at very low pressures, where the volume of gas molecules can be neglected.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the behavior of Z for all gases at high pressures?
questions.solution: At high pressures, all gases have Z values greater than 1, indicating that they are more difficult to compress.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How many types of curves are observed in the pV vs. p plots of real gases?
questions.solution: Two types of curves are observed in the pV vs. p plots of real gases.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: At what pressure range do the measured and calculated volumes approach each other in the pressure vs. volume plot?
questions.solution: At low pressures, measured and calculated volumes approach each other.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What do repulsive forces between gas molecules cause them to behave as at high pressure?
questions.solution: At high pressure, repulsive forces cause gas molecules to behave as small but impenetrable spheres.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In 1811, which scientist attempted to combine the conclusions of Dalton's atomic theory and Gay Lussac's law of combining volumes to propose a new law?
questions.solution: In 1811, the Italian scientist Amedeo Avogadro tried to combine Dalton's atomic theory and Gay Lussac's law to propose a new law, which is now known as Avogadro's law.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What does the Ideal gas equation suggest about the value of R?
options: R is always equal to 22.710981 L mol–1
R is equal to 8.314 J K–1 mol–1
questions.solution: The value of R in the ideal gas equation depends on the units in which pressure (p), volume (V), and temperature (T) are measured.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What does the value of 'a' in the van der Waals equation measure?
options: The magnitude of intermolecular attractive forces within the gas
The number of moles of the gas
questions.solution: The value of 'a' in the van der Waals equation measures the magnitude of intermolecular attractive forces within the gas.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: At what temperature does carbon dioxide remain in the gaseous state up to a pressure of 73 atmospheric pressure?
questions.solution: At 30.98°C, carbon dioxide remains a gas up to 73 atmospheric pressure.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of gas is called an ideal gas?
options: A gas that follows only Boyle's law
A gas that follows only Charles' law
A gas that follows Boyle's law, Charles' law, and Avogadro law strictly
A gas that follows none of the mentioned laws
questions.solution: A gas that strictly follows Boyle's law, Charles' law, and Avogadro law is called an ideal gas.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Under what conditions does Boyle's law hold true?
options: Constant temperature and number of moles
Constant volume and number of moles
questions.solution: Boyle's law holds true when there is a constant temperature and a constant number of moles of gas.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What term is used for the lowest hypothetical temperature at which gases are supposed to occupy zero volume?
questions.solution: The lowest hypothetical temperature at which gases are supposed to occupy zero volume is called Absolute zero.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the nature of the motion of gas particles?
questions.solution: The motion of gas particles as being random and in straight lines.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the measured volume at very high pressure in the pressure vs. volume plot?
options: It is less than the calculated volume
It is equal to the calculated volume
It is more than the calculated volume
questions.solution: At very high pressure, the measured volume is more than the calculated volume.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the SI unit of the coefficient of viscosity?
options: Newton second per square meter (N s/m^2)
questions.solution: The SI unit of the coefficient of viscosity is 1 newton second per square meter (N s/m^2).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How is the average speed of gas molecules calculated?
options: By measuring the speed of each molecule
By adding the minimum and maximum speeds
By taking the square of the speed values
By summing the individual speeds and dividing by the number of molecules
questions.solution: The average speed of gas molecules (uav) is calculated by summing the individual speeds (u1, u2, ...un) and dividing by the number of molecules (n).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: At what temperature does carbon dioxide remain as a gas only up to a certain point?
questions.solution: At 21.5°C, carbon dioxide remains as a gas only up to point B.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the temperature at which the clear boundary between the liquid and vapor phases disappears called?
questions.solution: The temperature at which the clear boundary between the liquid and vapor phases disappears is called the critical temperature.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the term for each curve in a graphical representation of Boyle's law at constant temperature?
questions.solution: Each curve in the graph corresponds to a different constant temperature and is known as an isotherm.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the initial reason a clear boundary is visible between the liquid and vapor phases when heating a liquid in a closed vessel?
options: The vapor becomes denser than the liquid
The density of the vapor decreases
questions.solution: Initially, a clear boundary is visible because the liquid becomes less dense as it is heated.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What effect does high altitude have on atmospheric pressure?
options: It has no effect on atmospheric pressure.
questions.solution: At high altitudes, atmospheric pressure is low.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: At the critical point, what happens to the horizontal portion of the isotherm?
questions.solution: At the critical point, the horizontal portion of the isotherm merges into one point.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Why is an ideal gas considered hypothetical?
options: It is extremely rare in nature
It has a very low boiling point
It is assumed to have no intermolecular forces between its molecules
It exists only at very high pressures
questions.solution: An ideal gas is considered hypothetical because it is assumed to have no intermolecular forces between its molecules.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What does the shape of the curve of isotherms of carbon dioxide at high temperatures look like?
options: It resembles that of an ideal gas.
questions.solution: At high temperatures, the shape of the curve of isotherms of carbon dioxide resembles that of an ideal gas.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the primary reason for the lower pressure exerted by real gases compared to ideal gases at high pressures?
options: The higher temperature of real gases
The difference in the molecular composition of real gases
The effect of molecular interactions due to molecular attractive forces
The lower number of gas molecules in real gases
questions.solution: The lower pressure exerted by real gases at high pressures is due to the effect of molecular interactions resulting from molecular attractive forces.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What property of liquids allows them to be poured and flow?
questions.solution: The free movement of molecules in liquids allows them to be poured and flow.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How do the speeds of gas particles change over time?
questions.solution: The speeds of gas particles go on changing constantly.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How are partial pressures defined in a mixture of gases?
options: The pressures exerted by reactive gases.
The total pressure of the mixture.
The pressures exerted by individual gases as if they were alone in the same volume.
The average pressure of all gases in the mixture.
questions.solution: Partial pressures in a mixture of gases are the pressures that individual gases would exert if they were enclosed separately in the same volume and under the same conditions of temperature.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is another name for the Kelvin temperature scale?
questions.solution: The Kelvin temperature scale is also called the Thermodynamic scale of temperature.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What happens to Z values above the Boyle point for real gases?
options: Z shows positive deviations from ideality.
questions.solution: Above the Boyle point, real gases show positive deviations from ideality, and their Z values are greater than one.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How does pressure arise in a gas?
options: From the movement of particles in straight lines
As a result of collisions between gas particles
questions.solution: The pressure in a gas arises as a result of collisions between the gas particles.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What holds the closely and slowly moving molecules of a gas together, leading to liquifaction?
questions.solution: Intermolecular interactions may hold the closely and slowly moving molecules together, leading to the liquifaction of a gas.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the term for the boiling temperature at 1 atm pressure?
questions.solution: The boiling temperature at 1 atm pressure is called the normal boiling point.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What specifically resists the movement of fluid layers past one another in terms of intermolecular forces?
questions.solution: Strong intermolecular forces between molecules hold them together and resist the movement of fluid layers past one another.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What does the horizontal portion of the isotherm at the critical point represent?
options: The melting point of carbon dioxide.
The boiling point of carbon dioxide.
The coexistence of gaseous and liquid carbon dioxide.
questions.solution: The horizontal portion of the isotherm at the critical point represents the coexistence of gaseous and liquid carbon dioxide.

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: When the temperature of an ideal gas is increased from $27^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ to $927^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, the kinetic energy will be
questions.solution:
Increase in temperature of ideal gas from $27^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ to $927^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\therefore$ Increase in $K E=\frac{3}{2} R T\begin{aligned} T_1 & =27+273 \\ & =300 \mathrm{~K} \\ T_2 & =927+273 \Rightarrow=1200 \mathrm{~K} \\ \therefore \quad K E_1 & =\frac{3}{2} \times R \times 300 \mathrm{~K} \\ K E_2 & =\frac{3}{2} \times R \times 1200 \mathrm{~K} \\ \text { So, } \frac{K E_2}{K E_1} & =\frac{\frac{3}{2} \times R \times 1200 \mathrm{~K}}{\frac{3}{3} \times R \times 300 \mathrm{~K}}=4\end{aligned}$
Hence kinetic energy is increased four times.
